questions.stem: What is the chemical name for the common household compound known as 'Baking Soda'?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Baking soda is Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO3). When mixed with an acid (like buttermilk or vinegar) in baking, it releases carbon dioxide gas, causing dough to rise and become fluffy.
DECOY BUSTING: Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3) is 'Washing Soda', used in laundry. Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3) is limestone/chalk. Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH) is caustic soda (lye), used in soap making.
EXAM INSIGHT: Baking soda is also an excellent mild antacid for heartburn because it safely neutralizes excess stomach acid.

questions.stem: Which process is used to harden liquid vegetable oils into solid fats (like margarine or vanaspati ghee)?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Hydrogenation is the chemical process of forcing hydrogen gas into unsaturated liquid oils (like soybean or sunflower oil) at high temperatures and pressures, usually with a nickel catalyst. This saturates the carbon bonds, turning the liquid oil into a semi-solid fat (margarine).
DECOY BUSTING: Pasteurization is heating milk to kill bacteria. Saponification is making soap from fats and lye. Vulcanization is hardening rubber using sulfur.
EXAM INSIGHT: Partial hydrogenation is notorious for creating 'trans fats', which are highly detrimental to cardiovascular health as they raise bad LDL cholesterol.
